[Date]

Ambetter from Superior HealthPlan  
Appeals Department  
5900 E. Ben White Blvd.  
Austin, TX 78741  

Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization  
Member: Sawyer Hayes  
Member ID: W641457203  
Reference number: POC-DDD103990C-51911  
Requested service: Arthroscopic shoulder labral/instability repair  
CPT: 29806  
Date of denial notice: August 14, 2026  

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of authorization for CPT 29806. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The clinical records do document a substantial and appropriately targeted course of non-operative treatment, together with persistent instability, recurrent dislocations, objective examination findings, and imaging-confirmed structural injury.

The clinical information is as follows:

- I have had approximately 12 months of recurrent shoulder-instability episodes with apprehension.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy from May 5, 2026, through July 14, 2026, totaling 16 visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents treatment focused on rotator-cuff and scapular-stabilizer strengthening, together with activity modification.
- I used NSAIDs for approximately six months during symptom flares.
- A July 1, 2026 MR arthrogram demonstrated an anteroinferior labral tear, also known as a Bankart lesion, with a small Hill-Sachs lesion. Glenoid bone loss was under 10 percent, and the rotator cuff was intact.
- I have experienced three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptoms began. The most recent dislocation required reduction in the emergency department.
- The instability materially limits function: I avoid overhead reaching and cannot return to work involving lifting.
- Examination demonstrated positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing.
- Strength remains full, but the structural instability and recurrent dislocations persist despite treatment.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use disorder. I am a non-smoker, and my BMI is 29.

The publicly available Evolent shoulder-arthroscopy guideline identified by the plan lists CPT 29806 under shoulder labral repair. The guideline states:

“Clinical correlation of individual’s subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)”

and:

“Individual has limited function (age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational, or athletic).”

It also states:

“Clinical notes should address: Symptom onset, duration, and severity; Loss of function and/or limitations; Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable).”

The guideline identifies non-operative measures that may include:

“Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program; Rest or activity modification; Application of heat or ice; Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated); Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial, intra-articular space, or bicipital groove.”

The submitted records address these requirements. They document prolonged symptoms, substantial functional limitations, objective examination findings, imaging-confirmed pathology, 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy with 16 completed visits, activity modification, and six months of NSAID use. A corticosteroid injection was not clinically indicated for recurrent anterior instability caused by a Bankart lesion and therefore should not be treated as a reason to deny authorization where the other conservative measures have been completed and failed.

The clinical record further demonstrates that conservative treatment has not corrected the instability. I have sustained three anterior dislocations, including one requiring emergency-department reduction, and remain unable to perform overhead or lifting work. The MR arthrogram and examination findings correlate with the requested stabilization procedure.

I request that Ambetter from Superior HealthPlan overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29806. In the alternative, please provide the exact version of the Evolent guideline and the specific CPT-29806 clinical subsection applied to this request, identify every item of documentation considered missing, and provide the complete clinical-review rationale.

Please treat this as a standard appeal. If my treating surgeon determines that delay could seriously jeopardize my health or ability to function, please also consider this request for expedited review.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Hayes  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]  

Enclosures:

- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 visits from May 5, 2026, through July 14, 2026  
- MR arthrogram report dated July 1, 2026  
- Orthopedic examination and office notes  
- Emergency-department record for the most recent dislocation and reduction  
- Medication history documenting NSAID use  
- Surgeon’s letter of medical necessity  
- Copy of the denial notice dated August 14, 2026
